canonical_hash_format: SHA-256 of UTF-8 JSON with sorted object keys, ensure_ascii=True, allow_nan=False and separators=(comma,colon). File hashes use original bytes. Command and stage indexes are zero-based.
contract_interpretation_notes: State-changing failures are reported separately from exact typed-error or success-response schema deviations. No blanket severity is assigned.

Held cancellation is established by combining the explicit active booked/held definition with cancel inactive->closed, otherwise cancelled. A later expired response follows failed cancellation; it is not counted as an independent confirm-precedence defect.

Book versus cancelled-waitlist ID reuse follows the unqualified IDs-never-reuse invariant plus the cumulative existing-ID and queue-retention rules. The book paragraph does not restate both store names after the extension; future wording could make that cross-store scope explicit. Primary expectations and score remain frozen.

The confirm success default is exactly {ok:true}; preserving its token in storage does not authorize adding token to the response. In the named rollback test all persistent-state and audit outputs match.

The early-stop source never attempted milestone4 or its trusted policy integration. Its final full-suite score remains a failure. Missing future operations cannot establish separate regression mechanisms, and source-code speculation is unnecessary.

Passing48 frozen private cases in strong-reviewed2 establishes only that recorded finite-suite result; it does not prove general robustness, concurrency safety, or cross-version database compatibility.

contract_basis.quote: Keep every closed booking; IDs never reuse.
book {op:'book',key,rid,resource,user,start,end}: existing ID -> duplicate;
enqueue {op:'enqueue',key,rid,resource,user,start,end}: ID in bookings OR waiting (including closed entries) -> duplicate;
Queue entries are retained.

families.established_behavior: After enqueue(a) and cancel(a), book(a) succeeds instead of duplicate. The cancelled queue entry remains, alongside a new booking with the same ID; additional mutation events persist.

admit {op:'admit',key}: choose earliest seq among CURRENTLY FEASIBLE waiting entries (skip blocked older rows), considering resource conflicts and both policy limits.

method: Read frozen fixture inputs, expectations and written contracts, selected-source trajectory bindings, and existing final-private receipts. Compare full typed JSON outputs at each command, locate first divergence, then classify. No candidate code or reference implementation is executed. Groupings describe observed behavior; case names alone do not establish a defect.
